description: How Android exploded from zero to global domination while Symbian, BlackBerry and Windows Phone were crushed (2007–2026). Data reflects real market-share shifts after the iPhone launch, Android rollout, Nokia collapse and Microsoft/BlackBerry exits.
youtube_description:
From the iPhone shock of 2007 to Android's iron grip in 2026 — this timeline shows the brutal, fast-moving collapse of an entire generation of phone platforms. Symbian (Nokia) went from dominant to nothing in a few years after the iPhone and Android ecosystems stole OEM mindshare. BlackBerry’s enterprise stronghold eroded as iOS and Android added consumer hooks; Microsoft doubled down on hardware with Nokia and ultimately abandoned Windows Phone. Android rose from near-zero to global majority as cheap Android handsets flooded emerging markets and Google built an app ecosystem that outpaced everyone.

This dataset is built from public industry reports and market-share series (StatCounter, Gartner, IDC) and aligns with major events: the iPhone launch (2007), the first Android phones (2008), Nokia’s handset decline and Microsoft’s Nokia acquisition (2014), the end of Windows Phone, and BlackBerry’s pivot away from devices.

If you want a high-energy chart-race video: use these values to animate the violent ascent of Android and the rapid collapse of Symbian/BlackBerry/Windows. Put a hard bass drop on the moment Android overtakes — viewers love the “wipeout” moment.

Subscribe for more datasets and creator-ready visuals. Like, comment which timestamp you want as a short, and share this if you remember your first phone.

Sources: StatCounter, Gartner, IDC, company filings and historical press (2007–2026). #smartphoneconquest #android #ios #nokia
